subject: Media Literacy
title: Recognizing Opinion vs. News
description: A 60-second lesson on Recognizing Opinion vs. News.

hook.text: Tucker Carlson's lawyers argued in court that no reasonable viewer would take his show as factual news.

buildup.text: News reports facts. Opinion interprets them. The problem is when opinion is presented as straight news.

discovery.text: News uses neutral language and attributes claims. Opinion uses first person and emotional framing.

twist.text: Many viewers can't tell the difference — 24-hour channels mix news and opinion in the same broadcast.

climax.text: If a news program makes you angry, it's probably opinion. News informs; opinion provokes.

punchline.text: News tells you what happened. Opinion tells you how to feel about it.

quiz.question: How can you distinguish news from opinion?
options: News is always on the front page
News uses neutral language while opinion uses emotional framing
